words.definition: a group of similar cells and associated material working together to perform a function
words.example: Muscle tissue consists of cells specialized for contraction.

words.definition: a structure made of multiple tissue types working together for particular functions
words.example: The heart is an organ composed of several tissue types.

words.definition: a group of organs that coordinate to perform major body functions
words.example: The digestive system is an organ system.

words.definition: the body system that rapidly detects stimuli, processes information and coordinates responses using neurons
words.example: The nervous system can coordinate rapid responses to environmental change.

words.definition: the system of glands and cells that releases hormones into body fluids to coordinate functions
words.example: The endocrine system often controls slower, longer-lasting responses.

words.definition: the brain and spinal cord
words.example: The central nervous system processes sensory information.

words.definition: the main organ of the nervous system in vertebrates, responsible for integrating information and coordinating many responses
words.example: Different regions of the brain carry out specialized functions.

words.definition: a cord of nervous tissue connecting the brain with peripheral nerves and coordinating some reflexes
words.example: A reflex can be coordinated through the spinal cord without conscious processing.

words.definition: a neuron that carries information from a receptor toward the central nervous system
words.example: A sensory neuron carries signals from a pain receptor.

words.definition: a neuron that carries signals from the central nervous system to an effector
words.example: A motor neuron can stimulate skeletal muscle contraction.

words.definition: a bundle of nerve fibres enclosed by connective tissues in the peripheral nervous system
words.example: A peripheral nerve may contain both sensory and motor fibres.

words.definition: the neural pathway that produces a rapid automatic response to a stimulus
words.example: A withdrawal reflex uses a reflex arc.

words.definition: a brain region important in coordination, balance and fine control of movement
words.example: The cerebellum helps coordinate precise movements.

words.definition: a hormone whose secretion varies with the light-dark cycle and helps regulate circadian rhythms
words.example: Melatonin levels usually rise during the biological night.

words.definition: an approximately 24-hour biological cycle
words.example: Sleep and wakefulness follow a circadian rhythm.

words.definition: a hormone and neurotransmitter that helps prepare the body for rapid action during stress
words.japanese: エピネフリン・アドレナリン
words.example: Epinephrine can increase heart rate during a stress response.

words.definition: a brain region that links nervous and endocrine control and regulates many homeostatic processes
words.example: The hypothalamus helps regulate body temperature and hormone release.

words.definition: an endocrine gland beneath the brain that releases hormones controlling several body functions and glands
words.example: The pituitary gland releases hormones under hypothalamic control.

words.definition: a sensory receptor that detects changes in blood-vessel stretch related to blood pressure
words.example: Baroreceptors help regulate blood pressure.

words.definition: a sensory receptor that detects changes in chemical concentration or composition
words.example: Chemoreceptors can detect changes in carbon dioxide or pH.

words.definition: a network of neurons within the digestive tract that coordinates digestive activity
words.example: The enteric nervous system helps control gut movement.

words.definition: a control mechanism in which a response counteracts a deviation from a set range
words.example: Negative feedback helps keep internal conditions relatively stable.

words.definition: a biological agent capable of causing disease
words.example: Viruses, bacteria, fungi and some protists can act as pathogens.

words.definition: a disease caused by a pathogen that can be transmitted directly or indirectly
words.example: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by a virus.

words.definition: a structure that prevents pathogens from entering body tissues
words.example: Intact skin forms a physical barrier against pathogens.

words.definition: the protective outer covering of the body that blocks entry of many pathogens
words.example: The skin barrier is strengthened by tightly packed cells and keratin.

words.definition: a moist epithelial lining that secretes mucus and protects body passages
words.example: Mucous membranes trap pathogens in the respiratory tract.

words.definition: non-specific defence mechanisms present before exposure to a particular pathogen
words.example: Phagocytosis is part of innate immunity.

words.definition: specific immunity that develops through recognition of particular antigens and can generate memory
words.example: Adaptive immunity can produce a faster response after repeated exposure.

words.definition: a molecule or molecular region recognized as foreign or specific by the adaptive immune system
words.example: An antigen on a pathogen can stimulate lymphocyte responses.

words.definition: a specific immunoglobulin protein that binds to a particular antigen
words.example: Antibodies can neutralize pathogens or mark them for destruction.

words.definition: a white blood cell involved in adaptive immune responses
words.example: B and T cells are types of lymphocyte.

words.definition: a cell that engulfs and digests particles, microbes or cell debris
words.example: A phagocyte can engulf bacteria by phagocytosis.

words.definition: a long-lived lymphocyte that enables a faster and stronger response to a previously encountered antigen
words.example: Memory cells are important for long-term immune protection.

words.definition: administration of antigenic material to stimulate protective adaptive immunity
words.example: Vaccination can generate memory cells without causing the full disease.

words.definition: a preparation designed to stimulate protective immunity against a particular pathogen or disease
words.example: A vaccine may contain weakened, inactivated or selected pathogen components.

words.definition: the ability to resist or control infection through body defences
words.example: Immunity can arise after infection or vaccination.

words.definition: the process of becoming protected against a disease, often through vaccination
words.example: Immunization programmes reduce transmission of many infectious diseases.

words.definition: a substance that kills bacteria or inhibits their growth
words.example: Antibiotics are ineffective against viruses.

words.definition: the ability of bacteria to survive or reproduce despite exposure to an antibiotic
words.example: Natural selection can increase antibiotic resistance in bacterial populations.

words.definition: an infectious disease that can be transmitted between non-human animals and humans
words.example: Rabies is a zoonosis.

words.definition: an occurrence of disease cases above the expected level in a population or region
words.example: A local epidemic may occur when a pathogen spreads rapidly through a susceptible population.

words.definition: an epidemic that spreads across many countries or continents and affects large numbers of people
words.japanese: パンデミック・世界的大流行
words.example: A pandemic involves widespread international transmission.

words.definition: a small cell fragment in blood that contributes to clot formation
words.example: Platelets become activated at damaged blood vessels.

words.definition: a blood protein involved in the reaction sequence that produces a clot
words.example: Several clotting factors activate one another during coagulation.

words.definition: a soluble plasma protein that is converted into fibrin during blood clotting
words.example: Fibrinogen circulates in blood before clot formation.

words.definition: an insoluble protein that forms a mesh in a blood clot
words.example: Fibrin fibres trap cells and strengthen a clot.

words.definition: an enzyme that converts fibrinogen into fibrin during blood clotting
words.example: Thrombin promotes formation of the fibrin mesh.

words.definition: a lymphocyte that can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells and memory B cells
words.example: A B lymphocyte can recognize a specific antigen.

words.definition: a T cell that coordinates adaptive immune responses by activating other immune cells
words.example: Helper T lymphocytes stimulate B-cell and other immune responses.

words.definition: an activated B-cell derivative specialized for secreting large amounts of antibody
words.example: Plasma cells release antibodies specific to an antigen.

words.definition: human immunodeficiency virus, a retrovirus that infects key immune cells and can lead to AIDS
words.japanese: HIV（ヒト免疫不全ウイルス）
words.example: HIV reduces immune function by damaging populations of helper T cells.

words.definition: acquired immunodeficiency syndrome, the advanced condition caused by severe immune-system damage from HIV infection
words.japanese: AIDS（後天性免疫不全症候群）
words.example: AIDS greatly increases vulnerability to opportunistic infections.

words.definition: indirect protection that occurs when enough individuals in a population are immune to reduce pathogen transmission
words.example: High vaccination coverage can contribute to herd immunity.

words.definition: an infection that occurs more readily when immune defences are weakened
words.example: People with severe immunodeficiency are vulnerable to opportunistic infections.
